title: Entropic Fluctuations in Quantum Statistical Mechanics: A Review
authors: Tristan Benoist, Laurent Bruneau, Vojkan Jakšić, Aannalisa Panati, Claude-Alain Pillet
abstract: The celebrated Evans--Searles, respectively Gallavotti--Cohen, fluctuation theorem concerns certain universal statistical features of the entropy production rate of a classical system in a transient, respectively steady, state. In this paper, we review and compare several possible extensions of these fluctuation theorems to quantum systems. We present, in an introductory way, the approach proposed in a recent series of works [Lett. Math. Phys. 114, 32 (2024): doi:10.1007/s11005-024-01777-0], [Rev. Math. Phys 38, 2461006 (2026): doi:10.1142/S0129055X24610063], [Commun. Math. Phys. 406, 201 (2025): 10.1007/s00220-025-05360-z] and [J. Math. Phys. 67, 022101 (2026): doi:10.1063/5.0311182] including a previously missing extension of the Gallavotti--Cohen (steady state) version of the FT to two-time measurement entropy production in the algebraic setting of quantum dynamical systems. We focus on the open quantum systems, where a small system interacts with several (infinitely extended) reservoirs, and discuss the following approaches: naive, two-time measurement, phase space contraction and ancilla state tomography. We review the connection with modular theory. The latter provides a way to extend the classical notions to the quantum domain. We discuss the quantum version of the principle of regular entropic fluctuations, introduced in the classical context in [Nonlinearity 24, 699 (2011): doi:10.1088/0951-7715/24/3/003]. Finally, we relate the statistical properties of these various notions of entropy production to spectral resonances of quantum transfer operators and apply this approach to a paradigmatic model of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics: the spin-fermion model. The results presented here shed a new light on the nature of entropic fluctuations in quantum statistical mechanics.
summary: This review compares multiple theoretical approaches for extending classical fluctuation theorems to quantum statistical mechanics. It develops the theory using tools like modular theory and spectral analysis, demonstrating how quantum systems exhibit entropic fluctuations. The work is significant for establishing the quantum generalizations of fundamental theorems governing non-equilibrium processes.
main_problem: The paper reviews and compares various extensions of classical fluctuation theorems (like Evans-Searles and Gallavotti-Cohen) to the quantum domain, focusing on entropic fluctuations.
main_result: It establishes connections between different quantum approaches (Two-Time Measurement, Ancilla State Tomography) and shows that under certain conditions, the Principle of Regular Entropic Fluctuations (PREF) holds, leading to quantum fluctuation theorems.
method: The analysis employs advanced theoretical tools including modular theory, spectral resonance theory applied to quantum transfer operators, and the framework of large deviation principles (LDP).
model_or_system: The focus is on open quantum systems where a small system interacts with external reservoirs. A paradigmatic model used for illustration is the spin-fermion model.
key_observables: Entropy production rate, relative entropy, and various entropic functionals ($F_{east}$, $F_{QPSC}$, $Q_{\omega,t}$).
important_parameters: The coupling constant ($\lambda$), the waiting time ($T$), and the measurement time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on assumptions ensuring reservoir ergodicity, regularity for analytic deformations of Liouvilleans, and the applicability of LDP theorems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reviewing classical theorems, then introducing the quantum framework, detailing and comparing multiple quantum approaches (2TM, QPSC, EAST), and finally applying the theory to the spin-fermion model using spectral resonance techniques.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a rigorous, modern theoretical framework for understanding non-equilibrium dynamics and fluctuation theorems in quantum systems, which is central to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
